evidence.summaryExcerpt: The 1941 walk: Velcro's own history says the idea came to him one day after he returned from a hunting trip with his dog in the Alps. He took a close look at the burs of burdock that kept sticking to his clothes and his dog's fur. Other sources place it in a forest or a hike in the woods, so the "Alps" detail comes mainly from Velcro's marketing and Wikipedia. The microscope discovery: Back home, de Mestral slipped a few burrs under a microscope and saw that their barbed, hook-like seeds meshed with the looped fibres in his clothes.

claimResults.note: Attributed to Velcro Companies' own account of its founder (Tier A for its own history, though promotional, as the summary notes); Wikipedia and swissinfo.ch (Tier B) are also in the list.
